kare01.title: Dating or just hanging out?
kare01.caption:
Movie night number nine, shared fries, they've met your plant. If you're guessing what this is, that's your sign you're allowed to ask.
Save this for the next couch night.

kare02.title: Introduced as "my friend"
kare02.caption: Being introduced as "my friend" can sting when you hoped for more. That sting is information. Tell them how it landed, then ask what they meant.

kare03.title: Month three, still no label
kare03.caption: Three months of dates and still no label? Time won't define it for you. A calm, honest conversation will, and you're allowed to start it.

kare04.title: Couple on Saturday, strangers by Monday
kare04.caption: Pancakes and matching scarves on Saturday, "busy week!" on Monday. Notice the pattern, name it kindly, and ask for the weekday version too.

kare05.title: Cropped out of the photo
kare05.caption: Always just an elbow in their photos? You don't need to be posted to feel secure. You need to know where you stand, so ask for a straight answer.

kare06.title: Do I get them a holiday gift?
kare06.caption: Five weeks in and frozen in the gift aisle? Skip the price spiral. Ask what they're doing for the holidays, and a small, thoughtful card is never wrong.

kare07.title: Everyone else already calls it a relationship
kare07.caption: When your friends already ask how your person is, they're seeing something real. If everyone can see it, the two of you can say it out loud.

kare08.title: Jealous with no "right" to be
kare08.caption: Feeling jealous when you're "not official" isn't a crime, it's a clue. Skip the tests. Tell them what you actually want with them.

kare09.title: Rehearsing the talk in the mirror
kare09.caption: Eleven rehearsals, one easel, one pillow scream. The real speech is short: I like you. I'd like more. You? Then listen to what they say.

kare10.title: "I'm not looking for anything serious." "Me neither!"
kare10.caption: Said "me neither" when you meant "me, very much"? Agreeing to less than you want isn't chill, it's hiding. You're allowed to say what you're looking for.

kare11.title: Only texts after midnight
kare11.caption: "hey stranger" at 12:47, silence at noon. Late-night texts can feel close. Notice who makes plans with you before noon.

kare12.title: Was that a date?
kare12.caption: "Wanna grab food?" No decoder ring needed. Just ask, "as a date?" Clarity is cute, and the answer might be the one you're hoping for.

kare13.title: Both waiting for the other one to say it
kare13.caption: Typing, deleting, sending "hey :)" while they do the exact same thing. You're both holding the same door. Someone has to go first, and it can be you.

kare14.title: When they say "I don't know"
kare14.caption: You finally asked and heard "idk." Thank them for being honest. "I don't know" is an answer for now, so get clear on what you need and say it kindly.

kare15.title: Hearing "just friends" with grace
kare15.caption: Asked, and heard "just friends." It's okay if that hurts. A kind no is still a clear one, and "thank you for telling me" keeps the friendship whole.

kare16.title: Six months of almost
kare16.caption: Six months of umbrellas, second coffees and almost-asks interrupted by a waiter, a sneeze and a bus. Wait for the answer. Guessing took months, asking took a minute.

kare17.title: The holiday party plus-one
kare17.caption: The invite says +1 and your mind throws three imaginary parties. Keep the ask to two lines: what you want, and a question. Ask before the party, not at the door.

kare18.title: The talk, from both sides
kare18.caption: Two apartments, two pillows, the same fear and the same rehearsed words. If you're scared to ask, they might be too. Your almost is their almost.

kare19.title: When the answer is no
kare19.caption: Virgo asks, Leo says no, honestly and kindly. Then a sad weekend, a friend with soup, and a dinner full of laughing. A clear no gives you your weekends back.

kare20.title: Pisces finally asks
kare20.caption: Thirty-seven tissues and three almost-asks later, Pisces says it plainly. Bring tissues for the answer. Ask first, cry after, happy tears included.
